newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-France sees room for one Euro plane-maker.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-France sees room for one Euro plane-maker.

text.p: New French Defence Minister Alain Richard was quoted on Thursday as saying there was room for just one plane-maker in Europe and that he saw a combined Dassault-Aerospatiale as simply a component of such a firm.

In testimony to the National Assembly Committee on Defence delivered on Wednesday and made public a day later, Richard added that the situation was different for defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF, which he said was important enough not to have to be submerged into a conglomerate.
"In the aerospace industry, it seems a given that there is room for just one plane-maker, civilian and military, in Europe," Richard told the assembly panel according to a statement on Thursday.
"Negotiations in search of agreements with the governments of other countries are fundamental, with the bringing together of Dassault and Aerospatiale a simple component," he said.
But in the defence electronics sector, he said it was not clear that just a single European firm was required.
"The position occupied by Thomson-CSF makes it big enough not to have to be a secondary player," he said.
European and U.S. aerospace executives have been anxious to know the new leftist government's plans for defence industry consolidation.

The previous centre-right government had planned to privatise state-owned Thomson-CSF and merge Dassault Aviation and Aerospatiale in moves seen as key to unlocking further European defence consolidation, needed to face up to competition from mega-mergers in the United States.
Dassault makes combat planes, while Aerospatiale derives some 70 percent of its revenues from making commercial jets for the Airbus Industrie consortium.
Richard said in his testimony that the new government, swept into power in a June 1 parliamentary election, might have to revise the 1997 defence budget but would not know for a few months.
He said the government had undertaken a budgetary review "which will be presented at the end of the summer and might entail some adjustments".
Budgetary changes might also be dictated by changes in strategic policy over the next five years, he added.
If budget changes were required, he pledged that any plans would be fully and openly debated beforehand.
France is under pressure to keep down public deficits down so that it can join a single Eurpean currency from 1999.
But new Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin has pledged to avoid new austerity measures in order to qualify for the euro from the start.

Questions have been raised over France's commitment to monetary union because Jospin has ordered an audit of the overall state of public finances and hitned that deficits would be higher than expected, possibly barring France from joining European monetary and economic union.
